title: monado-viture: Luma Ultra as a Monado OpenXR device on sfub
description:
# monado-viture: the Luma Ultra as a Monado OpenXR device on sfub

Goal: a working OpenXR path for the VITURE Luma Ultra on Linux through an
out-of-tree `xrt_device` driver in Monado, so the glasses are an HMD surface
rather than a phone-only accessory. sfub drives it; the Fold5 thin-client path
and UxSpace are untouched.

- driver + docs + scripts: `experiments/monado-viture/`
- Monado checkout: `/home/sf/workspace/monado` (patch APPLIED, base `e936b6a`)
- runtime shape: out-of-process. `scripts/build` -> `scripts/run-service` (the
  service owns the unix socket) -> `scripts/run-hello-xr`
- headless validation uses the compute compositor (`XRT_COMPOSITOR_COMPUTE=1`)

## milestones (measured 2026-09-28/29, commits 1a04a9e..dbc60b4)

| | milestone | state | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | build Monado on sfub without root | DONE | exit 0, zero warnings, patch APPLIED vs `e936b6a` |
| M1 | static VITURE HMD instantiates via OpenXR | DONE | `Head: 'VITURE (pid 0x0000)'`, 2 views, panel 3840x1200@90 sbs |
| M1 | hello_xr runs stereo against it | DONE | both swapchains 2688x1680, `XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED`, 0 errors, exit 0 |
| M2 | stereo actually reaches the panels | blocked | hardware gate |
| M3 | Carina 3DoF rotation drives HMD orientation | blocked | hardware gate |
| M4 | BeamNG native Linux OpenXR starts and tracks | not started | `scripts/run-beamng` refuses until M0-M3 are measured |
| M5 | Carina 6DoF translation | not started | 6DoF is the default path, unit unverified |
| M6 | recentering, prediction, latency tuning | not started | |

## blocking gate

The Luma is not attached to sfub, and the seat user cannot open its USB devnode
until the root-owned udev rule is in place:

    sudo cp experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
    sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

M2 and M3 carry `blocks` dependencies on the gate bead, so `br ready` stays
honest while the glass is off the desk.

## operational hazards found while measuring M0/M1

- **stale IPC socket.** A killed `monado-service` leaves
  `/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc`; the next start dies with `Address already in
  use`. `scripts/run-service` now clears a socket that no live process owns.
- **X connector-metadata flap.** After Vulkan/DRM work X reported
  `DP-0 disconnected ... 0mm x 0mm` (once a transient `3440/910x1440/381` where
  the EDID says `797x333`) while the kernel still reported `card1-DP-1 connected`
  with a valid EDID. Mode, refresh, layout, primary flag and 110x110 dpi were all
  unaffected -- only X's per-output metadata went stale. Cause unestablished;
  expect it again at M2.

## out of scope

Recentering/prediction/latency tuning (M6), any Android-side integration, and
anything that changes UxSpace or the Fold thin client. Failed or blocked work
stays open; the epic closes on operator acceptance of M2/M3.

## transport (2026-10-04)

The glasses are currently attached through an HDMI hub, not the vendor path: they
appear as a DRM/HDMI sink ("VITURE") on HDMI-0 while the USB side does not
enumerate. Enough to *reach the panels*, not enough for Carina.

- the hub declares a 300 MHz pixel-clock ceiling; native-rate stereo
  (3840x1200@90 ~ 441 MHz) is out of budget on it (see the transport survey bead)
- nvidia 595.84 refuses `xrandr --addmode` for any non-EDID timing on this output, and
  the DRM/KMS workaround is dead too: nvidia-drm reports every connector disconnected
  with 0 modes (NVKMS owns the real outputs) and X holds DRM master. Remaining routes:
  ModeValidation in xorg.conf + X restart, stopping X, or an adapter whose EDID already
  declares the wide timing. `tools/kms-probe.py` covers the no-X case.
acceptance_criteria: M2 and M3 measured on sfub with the glasses attached, and the operator accepts the result.

title: Recon: XR invariants, local display/GPU stack, Monado driver model, VITURE SDK, prior art
description:
Read the XR workspace rules, then establish the substrate before writing code:

- local: X11/NVIDIA/glasses/DRM/Vulkan state, including the pre-existing phantom
  1920x1200@90 HDMI-0 output
- Monado: how an out-of-tree `xrt_device` is registered and built (`XRT_BUILD_DRIVER_*`)
- VITURE: which Linux SDK pieces exist for Carina/pose, and what the native libs need
- prior art: Breezy / xr_driver / Monado branches touching VITURE

Findings landed in `experiments/monado-viture/docs/`.
acceptance_criteria: The build path, the driver insertion point and the SDK's Linux surface are known and written down; no unresolved how-would-this-attach question remains.
close_reason: recon complete; findings recorded in experiments/monado-viture/docs/

title: Transport survey: what the HDMI hub vs a real VR adapter can carry
description:
The channel between sfub and the Luma Ultra is not the vendor path right now: the
glasses hang off an HDMI hub/adapter and the USB path does not enumerate at all
(no 0x35ca device on the bus, no /dev/viture*, udev rule not installed).

## what the current hub declares (2026-10-04, RTX 4070, nvidia 595.84)

| property | value |
|---|---|
| EDID source | the hub, synthesized: vendor `CVT`, product 0x3133, serial 0x88888800, EDID 1.3, 160x100 mm, input byte 0x80 (no HDMI-a/b flag) |
| DTD0 (preferred) | 1920x1200 @ 90 Hz, 225.00 MHz (htotal 2000 x vtotal 1250) |
| DTD1 | 1920x1080 @ 60 Hz, 148.50 MHz |
| range limits | v 56-120 Hz, h 50-160 kHz, **max pixel clock 300 MHz** |
| driver-added modes | 1920x1200@120 (310.5 MHz -- over the cap), 1920x1080@120, 720x480, 640x480 |

## link budget for stereo (one frame carrying both eyes)

- 1920x1200@90 *per eye* as a native side-by-side frame (3840x1200@90) is
  ~441-450 MHz -- **47% over** the hub's declared 300 MHz ceiling.
- 3840x1200@60 (294 MHz) is the largest SBS timing that fits that ceiling.

## measured

- 1920x1200@90 sets and holds: 45 s watch, one monitor claimed, zero EDID
  re-probe warnings.
- 1920x1200@120 latches at X level (310.5 MHz). Over the cap, so whether the
  sink locks is unverified -- needs the eyes.
- custom SBS modelines cannot be attached through X: `--newmode` succeeds (modes
  0x322-0x327 persist on the screen) but `--addmode` returns `BadMatch` for every
  width tried (1600 / 1920 / 2560 / 3200 / 3840). nvidia 595.84 will not attach a
  timing it did not derive from the display's EDID/CVT list.

## consequence

Any wide/SBS timing must be set at the DRM level (Monado's display compositor, or
modetest, using the seat user's card0 access), not through X. X holds DRM master
on vt2, so a DRM mode set happens either on another VT or with X stopped.

## next

Repeat the same probe on the real VR adapter once it is plugged in. The
discriminator is its EDID: does it advertise an SBS timing, and is its max pixel
clock >= ~450 MHz?
acceptance_criteria: A written per-adapter verdict on whether native-rate per-eye stereo (1920x1200@90 each eye) can be carried, from the adapter's declared EDID limits plus a mode-set/lock test.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 AZ (measured):

Visual confirmation (operator, glasses on the hub): 1920x1200@90 displays the
normal GNOME desktop cleanly. First attempt to eyeball an SBS pattern failed for a
mundane reason -- xsetroot's root-window bitmap is covered by the desktop session,
so no pattern was visible. Not a signal problem.

Hz budget of THIS hub (the thing we are replacing):
- preferred/native: 1920x1200 @ 90 Hz, 225.00 MHz -- works, stable, verified by eye
- driver-offered: 1920x1200 @ 120 Hz = 310.5 MHz (already over the hub's own
  declared 300 MHz ceiling; lock quality untested)
- ceiling per the hub's EDID: 300 MHz
- native-rate stereo (3840x1200@90) needs ~441-450 MHz -> out of budget by ~47%
- largest in-budget stereo timing: 3840x1200@60 = 294.24 MHz

Verdict for the current hub: fine as a 1920x1200@90 2D display adapter; cannot
carry both eyes at native resolution and native refresh in one frame.
Replacement planned; unique VR adapter to be surveyed next against this baseline.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 ceiling probe (no root, no X restart):

1920x1200@120 = 310.5 MHz (10.5 MHz over the hub's declared 300 MHz cap) was set
through X and held 20 s with zero kernel warnings, then @90 restored cleanly. X-level
acceptance is not sink-level lock -- operator eyes decide.

Routes to a 3840-wide SBS test, both investigated:
- X: `--newmode` succeeds, `--addmode` returns BadMatch at every width (1600..3840);
  nvidia 595.84 attaches only EDID-derived timings.
- DRM/KMS: nvidia-drm reports all connectors disconnected with 0 modes while X drives
  HDMI-0 fine, and X holds master.
So this hub's ceiling is argued from its own EDID plus timing math, not a lock test.

DDC quality metric: nvidia-modeset logged 36x 'Unable to read EDID for display device
CVT VITURE (HDMI-0)' during attach, ~1/min, while X held a cached EDID. Flaky DDC.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 310.5 MHz margin result: 1920x1200@120 latched and displayed.
Operator could not distinguish 90 from 120 Hz by eye, but the image was present and normal
(no blackout, no rolling/garbling) for the 20 s hold. So the sink locks ~10.5 MHz above its
own declared 300 MHz ceiling -- the EDID cap is soft, not a hard wall. Refresh perception is
not a usable discriminator on these panels; 'image present at all' is.

Hub verdict so far: 1920x1200@90 native works cleanly; >=310 MHz still displays; DDC is flaky
(36 EDID read failures during attach); no SBS timing declared; 3840-wide impossible through X;
DRM route unusable while X owns the outputs.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 VR adapter swap (measured):

Transport changed from HDMI-through-a-cheap-hub to the real VR adapter:
- display now enumerates on DP-2 (DisplayPort alt mode), not HDMI-0. HDMI-0 is
  gone (0 EDID bytes, disconnected) -- the old hub was the HDMI sink.
- DP-2 mode list: 1920x1200@120/90/60 and 1920x1080@120/90/60. Still NO 3840-wide
  timing, and X exposes no EDID property for DP-2 (0 bytes), so its declared
  limits cannot be decoded the way the hub's could.
- vendor path is ALIVE now: 35ca:1104 'VITURE Luma Ultra XR GLASSES' (vendor
  interface, class 0, 7 endpoints) + 35ca:1102 microphone, plus a UVC camera
  (/dev/video0, /dev/video1) and a VITURE sound card.
- but all of those nodes are root-only: /dev/bus/usb/003/019,020 are root:root and
  a seat-user open returns EACCES; hidraw3/4 are 0600 root. The udev rule is the
  missing piece and it is not installed.

So: the VR adapter restores the vendor/USB path (Carina, mic, camera) but neither
adapter advertises a 3840-wide SBS timing -- per-eye native stereo, if it exists,
must be requested through the vendor interface rather than as a plain display
mode.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 STEREO MODE FOUND -- the per-eye question is a vendor mode, not an adapter bandwidth question.

The SDK exposes display modes (tools/viture-pose-dump --list-modes):
  0x31 1920x1080@60-2d   0x32 3840x1080@60-sbs  0x33 1920x1080@90-2d  0x34 1920x1080@120-2d
  0x35 3840x1080@90-sbs  0x41 1920x1200@60-2d   0x42 3840x1200@60-sbs 0x43 1920x1200@90-2d
  0x44 1920x1200@120-2d  0x45 3840x1200@90-sbs

0x45 is exactly '1920x1200 per eye at 90 Hz' as one 3840x1200 frame, 2 views. Setting it
over the vendor interface makes the sink RE-PRESENT its mode set to the host: DP-2's
declared size changed from the 1920x1200 placeholder to 160x100 mm and X now offers
'3840x1200 90.00 +' as preferred. The mode persists after the SDK process exits.

So the transport question becomes concrete: can the link carry 3840x1200@90 (~441 MHz
CVT-RB)? The VR adapter (DP alt mode) is being measured now. The cheap hub declared a
300 MHz ceiling and demonstrated lock at 310.5 MHz -- 441 would be ~42% beyond anything
it has shown, so the expectation is that the hub cannot, but that is now directly
testable by swapping it back and repeating this exact procedure.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 RESOLVED -- the VR adapter carries native-rate stereo; the cheap hub cannot.

Direct answer to the original question (1920x1200@90 per eye, i.e. 3840x1200@90
side-by-side = ~441-450 MHz on the wire):

- VR adapter (DP alt mode, glasses on DP-2): X latched 3840x1200@90 at 450.00 MHz
  (htotal 4000 x vtotal 1250), held, one monitor, zero kernel warnings, and the
  operator confirmed each eye gets one half of the frame. Native-rate stereo: YES.
- cheap HDMI hub: declared a 300 MHz ceiling and only ever demonstrated lock at
  310.5 MHz (1920x1200@120). 450 MHz is ~45% beyond anything it showed, and it
  advertised no SBS timing at all. Native-rate stereo: NO (declared limits).
- neither adapter advertises a 3840-wide timing by itself: the mode appears only
  after the vendor interface is told to use 0x45, at which point the sink
  re-presents its mode set to the host (DP-2's reported size changed from a
  1920x1200 placeholder to 160x100 mm and '3840x1200 90.00 +' appeared). So this
  was a vendor-protocol question, not purely a cable/bandwidth one.

Recommendation: keep the VR adapter for anything stereo; the hub is fine only as a
1920x1200@90 2D display path.

title: Scaffold experiments/monado-viture: driver tree, build, display safety
description:
Create the experiment tree and the safety rails:

- `src/` driver sources, plus `docs/`, `scripts/`, `tools/`, `udev/`
- `scripts/patch-monado.sh` (idempotent patch against a recorded base)
- `scripts/install-deps-local.sh` (private sysroot, no root)
- `scripts/restore-display` and a real topology snapshot before touching displays

This workstation's X topology has to survive every experiment, so restoring it
must be a two-command operation rather than an adventure.
acceptance_criteria: Tree exists; patch/install/build/restore scripts run; a topology snapshot is on disk before any display-affecting step.
close_reason: scaffold landed; snapshot taken, restore validated read-only

title: M0: build Monado on sfub (patched, private sysroot, no root)
description:
Patch a clean Monado checkout to register the VITURE driver, then build it
against a private sysroot -- no root, no system package changes.

`scripts/build` owns the whole path: patch -> configure -> ninja -> report.
Verified: exit 0, `ninja: no work to do` on re-run, zero warnings, both runtime
artifacts emitted (service binary + driver .so).
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/build` exits 0 with the patch applied and both artifacts present, with no root and no system-wide install.
close_reason: M0 measured: build exit 0, zero warnings, patch APPLIED vs e936b6a

title: M1: static VITURE HMD instantiates via OpenXR and hello_xr runs stereo
description:
With no vendor SDK and no hardware attached, the driver must still create a
usable HMD (`VITURE_NO_SDK=1`: static HMD, no tracking, panel 3840x1200@90 sbs,
2 views).

Then drive a real OpenXR client against the out-of-process service end-to-end:

    scripts/run-service
    scripts/run-hello-xr -g Vulkan --space Local

Verified: `Head: 'VITURE (pid 0x0000)'`, OrientationTracking + PositionTracking
reported, both swapchains 2688x1680, `XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED`, 0 errors, exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: hello_xr reaches XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED against the built runtime with two 2688x1680 swapchains and zero errors.
close_reason: M1 measured on the committed build path: FOCUSED, both swapchains 2688x1680, 0 errors, exit 0

title: Bug: run entry points were broken (4 defects) + add scripts/run-service
description:
Found by re-reading the committed scripts instead of trusting them:

- `run-hello-xr` pointed at a non-existent `hello_xr` path (OpenXR-SDK builds it
  under `build/src/tests/`), omitted the loader dir from `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and
  consumed its first positional as a binary path -- so the documented
  `run-hello-xr -g Vulkan` searched for a program literally named `-g`
- `scripts/build` summary `find` had an `-o` / `-maxdepth` precedence bug
- the `run-beamng` gate text claimed M0/M1 were unvalidated
- `restore-display` had no snapshot to restore to, so `restore` would have died

Plus `scripts/run-service`, because a killed service leaves
`/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc` and the next start dies with `Address already in
use` -- hit twice in one session.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented entry point runs end-to-end through the documented invocation, and a stale socket no longer blocks a restart.
close_reason: entry points fixed and re-verified end-to-end; wrapper proven on the real stale-socket case

title: Docs: architecture, coordinates, measurements
description:
Write down what the driver actually is while it is still fresh:

- `docs/architecture.md`: processes, socket, registry/plugin layout, compute vs display compositor
- `docs/coordinates.md`: pose / axis conventions and the verification procedure
- `docs/measurements.md`: M0/M1 evidence, hashes, and the exact commands used

Declared domain: the OpenXR/Linux driver experiment. The Fold5 thin-client path
and UxSpace are separate and must not leak into these docs.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture, coordinate conventions and the M0/M1 measurement record are in the repo and match observed behavior.
close_reason: docs written and cross-referenced from the experiment README

title: Hardware gate: attach the Luma Ultra to sfub and install the udev rule
description:
**Human action -- do not claim.**

The Luma Ultra is not attached to sfub, and the seat user cannot open its USB
devnode until the root-owned udev rule exists. M2 and M3 both block on this.

    sudo cp experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
    sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

then attach the glasses. Closing this bead asserts the rule is installed *and*
the device opened from the seat user's own session, with no root and no sudo
wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: Seat user opens the VITURE device on sfub after the udev rule is installed, without sudo.
close_reason: udev rule installed; seat user (uid 1000, ACL via uaccess) opens /dev/bus/usb/003/019+020, /dev/hidraw3+4, /dev/video0+1 RW with no root. Rule bug found and fixed in the same pass: the usb line carried ACTION=="add", which never fires on 'udevadm trigger' (default action=change), so usbfs nodes stayed root-only until the clause was dropped.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 attach state (gate stays OPEN):

- display path present: glasses enumerate as sink "VITURE" on HDMI-0 through an
  HDMI hub; 1920x1200@90 set and stable, X reports one monitor.
- USB/vendor path ABSENT: no 0x35ca device on the bus, no /dev/viture*, and the
  udev rule is not installed under /etc/udev/rules.d/.
- the seat user CAN open /dev/dri/card0 RW (logind ACL) -- so DRM-level mode sets
  are already possible without root. The rule is still required for the USB /
  Carina path that M3 depends on.

Gate stays open until the USB path works from the seat session.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 01:47 AZ -- gate is now ONE command from closing.

VR adapter attached (replacing the cheap HDMI hub). State:
- display: glasses enumerate on DP-2, driven at 1920x1200@90 (225.00 MHz), monitor
  claimed, no X errors.
- vendor USB path: ALIVE. 35ca:1104 'VITURE Luma Ultra XR GLASSES' (vendor
  interface class 0, 7 endpoints: interrupt IN 1024 B + bulk IN) and 35ca:1102
  'VITURE Microphone'. Also a UVC camera (/dev/video0,1) and a VITURE sound card.
- access: /dev/bus/usb/003/019 and /020 are root:root and a seat-user open returns
  EACCES; /dev/hidraw3,4 are 0600 root. /dev/video* and /dev/snd/* carry ACLs.

Remaining action (root, operator):

    sudo cp experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
    sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

Closing criterion unchanged: the seat user opens the VITURE device with no root
and no sudo wrapper.

title: M2: stereo reaches the Luma panels
description:
Once the glass is attached, get real per-eye output onto the panels instead of
the compute compositor's offscreen path:

1. `tools/viture-pose-dump --seconds 10 --json` -- confirm the device opens and streams
2. start the service on the vendor path (`VITURE_NO_SDK=0`) and run
   `scripts/run-hello-xr` with the display compositor
3. confirm distinct per-eye content and that 3840x1200 sbs actually scans out

Record the xrandr/DP state before and after: if X re-probes the connector, that
belongs in the epic's hazard list, not in silence.
acceptance_criteria: Both eyes show the expected distinct stereo content driven by hello_xr, and the workstation display topology is unchanged afterwards.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 transport constraints found before starting M2:

- X cannot set the mode we need: nvidia 595.84 refuses `--addmode` for any
  non-EDID timing on this output (`BadMatch` at every width tried), so a wide/SBS
  mode cannot be set through X at all. M2 must set it at the DRM level, which is
  where Monado's display compositor already operates and where the seat user has
  RW on card0. X holds DRM master on vt2, so that test runs on another VT or with
  X stopped.
- link budget: the current HDMI hub declares a 300 MHz pixel-clock ceiling;
  3840x1200@90 is ~441 MHz. Native-rate stereo is out of budget on this adapter.
  See xr-bi6.10 for the measurements.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
SUPERSEDES the DRM-level claim in the previous comment -- that route is dead on this host. Measured 2026-10-04:

- nvidia-drm (card0, the only DRM card) reports EVERY connector disconnected, 0 modes,
  mm=[0,0] -- including HDMI-A-1, which X is actively driving at 1920x1200@90 with a
  real EDID. nvidia-drm does not mirror the outputs NVKMS (the X driver) owns.
- X holds DRM master on card0 (a SET_MASTER attempt from the seat user returns EACCES),
  so a VT switch drops X's master -- but with the connectors reported disconnected there
  is nothing sensible to mode-set anyway.

Routes for a custom/wide timing here, cheapest first:
1. xorg.conf `Option "ModeValidation" "AllowNonEdidModes"` (root file + X restart) --
   keeps the NVKMS path that already works, lifts only the EDID restriction.
2. stop X and drive the GPU with nothing holding master.
3. an adapter whose EDID already declares the SBS timing (no override at all).
4. the vendor SDK's own display path.

Tooling: `tools/kms-probe.py` implements the DRM route honestly (enumerate + custom
timings via dumb buffers); keep it for the no-X case.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 M2 measured on real hardware (vendor path + XCB window target).

Chain, each link observed:
1. driver -> SDK: `viture_sdk_configure_display: display mode 0x45
   (3840x1200@90-sbs) confirmed` -- this is the native per-eye mode, 2 views,
   1920x1200 per eye at 90 Hz.
2. HMD: `viture_hmd_create: created: Luma Ultra, panel 3840x1200@90-sbs ...
   2 view(s), 90 Hz`, 64 mm lens separation, 42 deg FOV.
3. compositor viewports: views[0] x=0 w=1920 h=1200, views[1] x=1920 w=1920 --
   target 'xcb' overrides extents with (3840x1200). So the composite is a
   correct side-by-side pair, not a stretched single view.
4. X: Monado window 3840x1200 mapped, DP-2 at 3840x1200@90 (450.00 MHz), and the
   window itself carries rendered content (sampled and cropped per half).
5. client: hello_xr `Head: 'Luma Ultra'`, swapchains 2688x1680 per view,
   IDLE->READY->SYNCHRONIZED->VISIBLE->FOCUSED.

Blocking bug found and fixed in this pass: session creation deadlocked in our
own driver (non-recursive os_mutex taken twice around the SDK pose call). See the
commit that renamed poll_pose to viture_poll_pose_locked; M1 passed only because
the no-SDK path returned before the lock.

Two operational findings:
- `XRT_COMPOSITOR_LOG=debug` selects the deferred/windowed target path here and
  the window stays BLACK even though the client is FOCUSED and presenting. With
  LOG=info the same setup renders normally. Do not use debug level for visual
  bring-up.
- with VITURE_IPD_METERS=0 the view setup refuses: `failed to set up views`. Use
  a small non-zero separation if you want near-zero parallax.

PENDING operator eyes before this closes: the acceptance criterion asks for the
two eyes to show the expected stereo content.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 mode-state incident (display went blank on the panels; root-caused).

What happened, in order:
1. bring-up set the glasses to 0x45 (3840x1200@90-sbs) and the sink re-presented its
   mode set, so X offered 3840x1200@90 and the operator SAW the desktop split per eye.
2. a later attempt to restore a 2D desktop set the sink to 0x43 (1920x1200@90-2d).
   That succeeded, so the sink re-presented 1920x1200-only; X was still configured for
   3840x1200 and its cached mode list no longer contained that mode, so every later
   xrandr attempt failed with 'Configure crtc 0 failed: BadMatch'.
3. from then on set_display_mode fails in BOTH directions with ret=-3
   ('panel timing unchanged'), so the sink is stuck in 0x45 while X cannot drive it.
   Result: nothing scans out; panels black; the X root framebuffer still contains the
   expected content (verified by sampling the capture).

Evidence: 'display mode: before=0x45 set(0x43, 1920x1200@90-2d)=-3 after=0x45' and
the same for 0x45; service log 'WARN set_display_mode(0x45, ...) failed: -3'.

Also captured on the way: 'comp_window_xcb_init: Selected display 0 has no size --
Falling back to display 3: DP-2' (the XCB target's monitor index needed the fallback).

Recovery: replug the glasses (device-side reset + HPD so X re-reads the sink's EDID).

Follow-ups this exposed:
- our pose tool enables native DOF (set_dof_type_carina(1)) and then uses the
  NON-native set_display_mode; the vendor header is explicit that native mode needs
  xr_device_provider_native_set_display_mode with VITURE_NATIVE_DISPLAY_MODE_* values
  (a DIFFERENT numbering: 3D SBS 3840x1200@90 is 0x3B there, 0x45 in the standard set).
- the driver should never leave the sink in a mode X cannot follow; set_default_display_mode
  exists for the persistent case.
- pin the mode through the service path (which does apply it) rather than the tool, until
  the tool is fixed.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 recovery that works (replug) + mode-set semantics worth knowing.

After the operator replugged the glasses:
- the sink came up in its DEFAULT mode 0x31 (1920x1080@60) and X re-read the sink on
  HPD, so xrandr had a fresh valid list again.
- `--set-mode 0x45` then returned 0, where it had returned -3 for every attempt while
  the device was pinned. So the -3 was a device-side state, not a bad argument.
- ASYNC semantics: get_display_mode immediately after the set still reported the old
  0x31, while X a few seconds later showed '3840x1200 90.00*+' and had selected it as
  current. Do not read the immediate read-back as the outcome; watch X + the sink.

Verified end state: sink in 3840x1200@90-sbs, X screen 3840x1200, and the stereo test
pattern's five elements sampled at their exact expected coordinates in the root
capture (yellow/green/magenta squares + both white edge bars).

Tooling improved in the same pass: viture_mode_native_equiv() maps standard mode ids
into the native opcode space and the pose tool grew --get-mode, so a device in native
DOF mode can be switched correctly instead of silently failing.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 state after the thrash: GPU display engine wedged, sink reverted.

- nvidia-modeset logs 'ERROR: GPU:0: Idling display engine timed out' every ~4 min
  (first at 03:50, immediately after the failed mode attempts). X can no longer
  configure the CRTC on DP-2 at all: every xrandr mode set returns
  'Configure crtc 0 failed: BadMatch', including 1920x1080.
- the glasses reverted on their own to their default 0x31 (1920x1080@60-2d):
  '--get-mode' reports standard=0x31. So the 0x45 set reported ok, landed, and did
  not persist across the churn.
- meanwhile X still thinks the output is 3840x1200, which is why the panels are dark
  even though the framebuffer has content.
Recovery from here needs the X/GPU display state rebuilt (X restart or reboot); a
replug alone no longer helps because the engine itself is stuck.

Tooling landed in this pass (compiled, not yet exercised against a healthy device):
- viture_mode_native_equiv(): standard mode id -> native (Gen2) opcode space.
- pose tool: --get-mode (fast, standard query) and --native-probe (opt-in; the
  native queries DO NOT RETURN on a Carina device, so they must never be in the
  default path). Set failures now print the code plus the pinned-device hint.
- known wart: the tool's SDK teardown can stall for >15 s ('[CARINA] pause') when the
  device is in a bad state; use timeout and line-buffered output when scripting it.

title: M3: Carina 3DoF rotation drives HMD orientation
description:
Feed the Carina pose stream into HMD orientation and prove the axes are right,
not merely present:

1. characterise the stream: `tools/viture-pose-dump --seconds 10 --json`
2. `scripts/test-coordinates` (offline axis / yaw-pitch-roll units) must pass
3. drive rotation and watch the HMD orientation respond with the correct sign and
   axis -- no inversion, no swapped axes

The axes procedure in `docs/coordinates.md` is the acceptance protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Yaw/pitch/roll from the glasses reproduce in the HMD pose with correct signs and axes, per the documented procedure.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 Carina pose status.

The deadlock fix unblocked session creation, but the vendor pose path is still
failing inside the service: `[I][libglasses] CarinaDeviceProvider get GL pose
failed: -1` repeats, and at bring-up `viture_sdk_recenter` could not read a pose
to set the origin (ret -3). The SDK itself starts fine (vendor 2.4.0 ready, 6DoF,
device_type=2, Carina VIO threads running: MsckfVio/ImageProcessor/LocalMapping).

tools/viture-pose-dump against the same device DOES stream samples (~120 Hz,
1197 in 10 s) but every sample was identity with status=1 -- consistent with a
VIO that has not produced a solved pose yet, not necessarily a driver fault. So
the next M3 step is the axis/rotation procedure (rotate the glasses by hand,
watch yaw/pitch/roll move) with the service stopped, since two SDK clients
contending for the device is not a supported configuration here.

Note for whoever picks this up: pose-dump needs the SDK's own libs on the loader
path (LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<sdk>/x86_64) because libcarina_vio is dlopen'd and the
caller's DT_RUNPATH is not transitive -- without it you only get
'libopencv_highgui.so.4.2: cannot open shared object file'.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-04 pose stream characterised: the blocker is VIO convergence, not prediction.

Ran the pose tool at three prediction horizons against the attached glasses:
  --predict 0.0 / 0.02 / 0.05  ->  identical results every time:
  samples=598 failures=2 unstable=598 measured rate=120.00 Hz over 4.975 s
So prediction is NOT what makes the in-service calls fail (hypothesis tested and
disproved); the pose API works, returns ~120 Hz, and flags EVERY sample unstable with
an identity pose. 'unstable' is the SDK's own status, i.e. Carina's VIO has not
converged -- the numbers are not a driver mapping bug, the input is not good enough
yet.

Most likely cause at this desk: the tracking cameras have nothing textured/in the
field of view while the glasses sit still on the desk (VIO needs visual features and
some motion). Remaining M3 work is therefore:
  1. operator holds/wears the glasses and looks around a lit, textured room,
  2. rerun tools/viture-pose-dump and watch 'unstable' -> 'stable',
  3. then the axis procedure from docs/coordinates.md: yaw on turning, pitch on
     nodding, roll on tilting, no inversion, no swapped axes.
'failures=2' per 5 s is a separate, minor matter (2 in 598); the service's log shows a
higher failure rate, consistent with its pose calls contending with the SDK's USB
traffic rather than anything about prediction.

Reminder: this test needs no display at all -- it runs over USB, so a wedged X does
not block it.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-07 3DOF POSE IS ALIVE. M3 is unblocked; 6DOF is a separate (camera) problem.

Root-caused the identity-pose mystery by reading the vendor's own demo source, which
ships with the SDK (glasses-demo-src.zip -> glasses-demo/carina_camera.h/main.cpp):

- The demo registers the Carina stereo camera callback BEFORE start(), with the comment
  'the Carina VIO engine captures the callback pointer at start time'. Our tool never did.
  Fixed: xr_device_provider_register_callbacks_carina(h, NULL, NULL, NULL, cb) before
  start, plus a frame counter so the missing input is visible.

Measured, same device, same 10 s, back to back:
  3DoF (set_dof_type_carina(0)): stable=1078 unstable=120 (90.0% stable), yaw
    -0.16..1.02, pitch -0.04..0.46, roll 0.00..3.03 deg while the glasses sat still.
  6DoF (set_dof_type_carina(1)): stable=0 unstable=1198 (0.0%), all components exactly
    zero, AND 'stereo camera frames delivered: 0'.

So: 3DoF uses the IMU and works. 6DoF needs the Carina VIO, which has NO input because
the stereo camera stream never reaches the host -- registration succeeded (ret 0) but no
frames arrive. That is exactly M3 vs M5 on the roadmap: M3 is now reachable, M5 needs the
camera path solved separately (candidates: an explicit stream enable, a wear/state gate,
or the demo's opt-in preview path -- camera_bg is the RGB/UVC camera, not this pair).

Next M3 step: guided axis check with the glasses worn (turn -> yaw, nod -> pitch,
tilt -> roll), then feed the pose into the stereo demo renderer so the scene turns with
the head.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
2026-10-07 3DoF verified on real motion (M3's core).

Operator moved the glasses in a deliberately random order over a 50 s 3DoF capture
(5998 samples, --json). Analysis:
- pose_status: 100% stable from window 2 onward; only the first 2 s window was 51%
  stable, which matches the SDK's own wording for pose_status: '1 = unstable (may
  occur briefly after device start)'. So the startup transient is expected, not a fault.
- real motion was tracked on all three axes: yaw spans up to 175 deg, pitch 127 deg,
  roll 213 deg within 2 s windows, while position stayed exactly zero (3DoF does not
  track position -- correct for set_dof_type_carina(0)).
- because the order was random, several axes move in one window; a clean per-axis
  attribution needs an ordered run, which is what the next capture does.

Sign/axis mapping is being verified perceptually rather than numerically: the head-
tracked version of the stereo demo (pose -> camera yaw/pitch/roll in
tools/make-stereo-demo.py) lets the operator see whether turning the head turns the
scene the way a fixed world should.

title: CARINA STEREO SPATIAL SENSING
description:
Calibrate and expose the Luma Ultra Carina grayscale stereo cameras as a
reusable spatial sensing substrate for hand tracking, stereo depth, and
Monado/OpenXR hand tracking.

Does NOT block monado-viture HMD display / head-pose bring-up.
monado-viture remains: display -> head pose -> 6DoF -> OpenXR HMD.
This epic: calibrated stereo -> depth -> hand skeletons -> XR_EXT_hand_tracking.

These are stereo TRACKING cameras, not depth cameras. Depth is derived
downstream.

## Measured substrate (2026-09-30 / 2026-10-01)

One Carina XRDeviceProvider on USB 0x35CA:0x1104:
- stereo grayscale callback 640x480 ~25 Hz (L0+R0; L1/R1 unused on this firmware)
- pose ~25 Hz, imu ~1 kHz, vsync-ish ~60 Hz
- same native handle
- RGB 1080p is a distinct Sonix UVC path (0x0C45:0x636B)
- camera sdk_ts jumps onto CLOCK_MONOTONIC at seq 6 (see docs/carina-measurements.md)
- factory calib: outcome B, cache/carina empty (docs/carina-calibration.md)

Left and right fisheye cover the natural hand-manipulation volume with
large overlap. Carina grayscale capture did not light the central RGB
LED on the tested unit (measured behavior, not a privacy guarantee).

## Work now

- .1 .2 .3 closed.
- .4 tooling exists (`console/recorder/carina_calib.py`); synthetic selftest
  PASS. Not complete until a real ChArUco SENSOR session is solved.
  Do not invent metres.
- .10 cross-host Android vs Linux parity is READY by graph but **must not
  open Carina USB while xr-bi6 owns the glasses**.

comments.author: sf
comments.text:
Host-side capture path found on sfub (2026-10-04) -- useful as an independent
reference for this epic, with one important limitation:

Attaching the Luma Ultra to sfub through the VR adapter (DP alt mode) enumerates
the glasses over USB and exposes, to the seat user:

- 35ca:1104 'VITURE Luma Ultra XR GLASSES' -- vendor interface (class 0, 7
  endpoints). This is the SDK/Carina transport.
- a UVC camera: driver uvcvideo, card 'USB 2.0 Camera', MJPG up to 1920x1080@30
  (25/20/15/10/5 also offered), nodes /dev/video0 + /dev/video1. That is the RGB
  camera (2.07 MP), reachable with plain V4L2 -- no SDK, no Android app.
- 35ca:1102 'VITURE Microphone' -- USB audio, standard ALSA card, plus hidraw.

LIMITATION: Carina grayscale is NOT a V4L2 device. The stereo tracking pair does
not appear here at all; it stays behind the vendor interface (SDK / carina_vio).
So host-side RGB capture is available as a reference/verification path, but
host-side Carina stereo still requires the SDK path this epic is already using.

Access: the seat user can open all of it RW (verified). This needed the udev rule
at experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules, installed on sfub today --
and the rule had a real bug: its usb line carried ACTION=="add", which never
fires on 'udevadm trigger' (default action=change), so the usbfs nodes stayed
root-only. Fixed. Anyone hitting EACCES on the glasses on a fresh box: that rule,
reinstalled, is the fix.

title: cross-host Carina parity: Android vs Linux
description:
Cross-host Carina parity: prove that Android SDK sensor sessions (`xr-carina-sensor-v1`) represent the same optical streams the Linux/Monado path will feed into Mercury.

One physical Luma Ultra. Compare Android (Fold recorder) vs Linux (sfub, seat-user USB after xr-bi6.7).

## HARDWARE RULE

READY by dependency graph, but **do not run the live-Carina section while xr-bi6 owns the attached glasses.** A single Carina/libglasses owner at a time. Linux live probe waits until bi6 releases `0x35CA:0x1104`. Offline work (this description, capture-format notes, comparison harness) may proceed.

## Compare

Same unit, both hosts:

- L0/R0/L1/R1 presence and nullness
- dimensions and byte format (8-bit gray 640×480 expected on Android)
- orientation, left/right ordering, frusta
- frame cadence
- startup behavior (incl. camera `sdk_ts` epoch jump observed on Android)
- SDK timestamps vs host `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`
- pose / IMU / vsync rates
- exposure controls
- device identity / calibration identity (`sn_hash`)
- crop / flip / rotation differences

Save representative L/R frame pairs from both hosts. Decide whether a deterministic host transform is required.

**Explicitly answer:** is an Android-derived calibration directly reusable on Linux frames?

No Mercury integration in this bead. No depth. No factory K/R/T invention.

## Non-goals

Does not block xr-wdw.4 / .5 / .6 / .7. Offline calibration, depth, and Mercury stay independently executable.
acceptance_criteria: Same physical Luma compared on Android vs Linux for L0/R0/L1/R1, size, byte format, orientation, L/R order, frusta, cadence, startup, SDK vs CLOCK_MONOTONIC, pose/IMU/vsync rates, exposure, identity, crop/flip/rotation. Representative frame pairs saved. Deterministic host transform decided. Explicit yes/no: Android-derived calibration reusable on Linux frames. No Mercury. Hardware section waits while xr-bi6 owns USB.
